title: Dedicated capacity decision matrix — Customer Jupiter
body:
Purpose and scope

This doc captures the decision matrix and workshop notes from the Customer Jupiter POC (Nov 2025–Feb 2026). Goal: recommend a Redwood Dedicated configuration (pool sizing + autoscaling policy + fallback tiers) that meets the customer's 99th percentile latency targets for chat and batch embedding workloads while controlling monthly GPU spend within their budget envelope.

High-level customer constraints and workload profile (as described in kickoff):
- Expected concurrency: 120 steady concurrent chat sessions during peak hour; each session averages 1.8 requests/minute in peak bursts.
- Chat request distribution: 65% short messages (~128 tokens), 30% med (~512 tokens), 5% long (~2048 tokens).
- Embedding jobs: scheduled nightly bulk runs (~250k texts total), and on-demand single-item embeddings (bursty daytime requests ~50 req/s).
- Latency SLOs: chat P99 <= 350 ms server-side generation (excluding network), embeddings P90 <= 200 ms for on-demand single-item.
- Data residency: must run in customer VPC; private deployment planned with Dedicated pool.
- Budget: target GPU spend <= $55k/month (initial).

Key performance assumptions and throughput baselines (empirical tests from our lab using customer's model variants):
- Model variants: jovian-7b-q8 (fast), jovian-13b-q4 (balanced), jovian-70b-q4 (high-quality).
- Measured tokens/s (steady-state, single A100-80GB equiv):
  - jovian-7b-q8: 6000 tokens/s (generation path optimized, KV cache hit)
  - jovian-13b-q4: 2200 tokens/s
  - jovian-70b-q4: 480 tokens/s
- Typical chat generation length per request: median 80 tokens output; embedding ops are model-agnostic and compute-bound per text size.

Sizing methodology (decision matrix inputs):
- Convert request mix into token demand per second at peak.
  - Chat peak calculation: 120 concurrent sessions * 1.8 req/minute = 216 req/minute = 3.6 req/s. With average output 80 tokens => 288 tokens/s just accounting output. Allowing for input tokens and system turns, use safety factor x3 => 864 tokens/s.
  - Add daytime on-demand embeddings: 50 req/s; assume each embedding CPU/GPU equivalent of 6ms on optimized L4-like accelerator; treat as 50 concurrent light workers but budget separately.
- Map token demand to equivalent GPU instances using the tokens/s baselines above.
- Allow headroom for spikes, warmup, and caching miss: +40% margin for peak.

Candidate pool architectures (short names used in matrix):
- Small-ML (cost-optimized): Pool of t3 A100-equivalent nodes; autoscale aggressively, small min size. Best for workloads dominated by embeddings and short chats.
- Balanced-Chat (recommended mid): Mix of A100-equivalents sized for jovian-13b-q4 peak, dedicated share for short chats, warm standby for 70b.
- Quality-First (high-cost): Majority capacity for jovian-70b-q4 to avoid fallbacks; higher baseline but lower routing complexity.

Decision matrix (scored across criteria: Latency SLO, Cost, Headroom, Operational complexity, Fallback risk)
- Small-ML: Latency SLO=2/5, Cost=5/5, Headroom=2/5, Complexity=2/5, Fallback risk=4/5 => Primary fit: embedding heavy customers with lower chat SLOs.
- Balanced-Chat: Latency SLO=4/5, Cost=4/5, Headroom=4/5, Complexity=4/5, Fallback risk=2/5 => Primary fit: Customer Jupiter profile.
- Quality-First: Latency SLO=5/5, Cost=2/5, Headroom=5/5, Complexity=3/5, Fallback risk=1/5 => Primary fit: customers prioritizing quality at higher cost.

Recommended configuration (Balanced-Chat) — concrete numbers and policies:
- Model mix served: default route to jovian-13b-q4; transparent fallback to jovian-13b-q4-quant (lower-memory variant) then to hosted-low-latency microvariant if Dedicated pool saturated. Keep jovian-70b-q4 in warm-standby (1 node) for scheduled high-quality jobs.
- GPU instance type (unit): A100-80GB equivalence (we provision using H100 reservations if available, cost-adjusted).
- Baseline pool sizing: 6 x A100-equivalent nodes (min=4, target=6, max=12)
  - Rationale: Using the jovian-13b-q4 throughput (2200 tokens/s per node), peak demand (864 tokens/s) => theoretic single-node can handle peak, but need concurrency isolation, KV cache fragmentation, and embeddings overhead. 6 nodes provides concurrency headroom for routing spikes and offloading nightly batch.
- Autoscaling policy (policy details to be configured in Redwood Console):
  - Scale up triggers: sustained CPU/GPU utilization > 62% for 90s OR queued request latency > 150ms for 30s. Scale increment: +1 node, cooldown 120s.
  - Scale down triggers: utilization < 28% for 5m AND average queue length <1. Scale step: -1 node, cooldown 300s.
  - Burst policy: Allow temporary burst to max=12 using burst credits from pooled excess and cloud spot capacity; bursts limited to 6 minutes per event unless manually approved.
- Warm standby for large model: Keep 1 x A100-equivalent reserved for jovian-70b-q4; scheduled warm-up windows before expected high-quality runs to avoid cold-start 30–90s penalties.
- Embedding strategy: Dedicated lightweight workers (can be CPU-backed for many short embeddings) with autoscale independent of chat pool. For 50 req/s on-demand and nightly 250k bulk, recommend small CPU cluster (4 vCPU units with autoscale to 12) and a separate GPU burst queue for embedding acceleration when batch jobs exceed window.

Cost estimate (ballpark monthly GPU spend)
- Assumptions: A100-equivalent list price (on contract) = $3.20/hour per node (sustained). Reserved discount scenarios included. (Note: adjust to customer's cloud pricing.)
- Baseline (min 4 nodes, average running 6 nodes across month due to utilization): 6 nodes * 24 * 30 * $3.20 = $13,824/month (raw). Add 20% infra & orchestration overhead => $16.6k.
- Burst headroom and reserved warm-standby (1 reserved node for 70b + average spot top-ups): add $3.2k => subtotal $19.8k.
- Additional Dedicated platform fee and support (Redwood enterprise add-ons): ~$8k/month (approx) depending on SLA tier.
- Estimated total month 1 (pilot): ~$28k/month.
- Scale scenario (sustained growth to double peak): expect running average of 10 nodes => 10*24*30*$3.20 = $23,040 + overheads => total ~ $42–48k/month.
- If customer requires Quality-First baseline (8–12 nodes for 70b capacity), cost can exceed $70k/month.

Notes on sensitivity and tradeoffs
- Quantization and kernel-level optimizations can increase tokens/s by ~15–45% depending on model and kernel maturity; that reduces node count materially. Prioritize model quantization work in parallel to reduce committed capacity.
- Embedding CPU-path: offloading most short embeddings to CPU/NPU reduces GPU pressure. Estimate $2–5k/month savings if embeddings fully batched on CPU clients.
- Spot/Preemptible capacity can reduce burst cost but increases fallback complexity and tail-latency jitter. Recommend using spot only for non-latency-critical batch jobs.

Operational runbook (short):
- Day 0 (pilot): Deploy Balanced-Chat pool with min=4/target=6/max=8; enable tracing and token-level cost dashboards; run smoke tests with production-like traffic generator; validate P99 < 350ms.
- Week 1: Run 3 scheduled spike tests (2x expected peak) to verify autoscaling behavior; measure cold-start for warm-standby 70b; capture KV cache hit rates.
- Week 2–4: Iterate min/target/max and scale cooldowns based on observed queue latency; apply quantization patch if safe.
- Escalations: If P99 exceeds 500ms for two consecutive spike tests, trigger fallback to hosted microvariant and instantiate emergency +2 nodes in Dedicated pool.

Open questions for Customer/Next steps
- Confirm model variant acceptance: is jovian-13b-q4 acceptable as default quality? If not, we need to shift sizing and cost expectations.
- Obtain customer's actual cloud GPU pricing or preferred instance family (H100 discounts, committed use).
- Clarify embedding SLA for on-demand items (P90 target currently assumed).
- Approve burst minute policy and maximum monthly burst budget.

Action items (owners)
- Priya: finalize baseline pool config and submit proposal for customer approval (due 2026-02-20).
- Eli: run 2x spike stress tests against jovian-13b-q4 on Dedicated staging (due 2026-02-28).
- Carlos: quantify expected cost delta if H100 reserved pricing used and produce updated sheet (due 2026-02-25).
- Sana: prepare rollback/fallback playbook for hosted fallback route and test end-to-end latency.
summary: Workshop notes and recommended Dedicated pool (Balanced-Chat) for Customer Jupiter: baseline 6 A100-equivalent nodes (min4,max12), autoscale policies, warm-standby for 70b, estimated pilot cost ~$28k/mo, growth scenario ~$42-48k/mo. Next steps include pricing confirmation and spike tests.
